newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu sees rising zinc, nickel prices.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu sees rising zinc, nickel prices.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy said on Monday zinc and nickel prices are likely to rise in the next few years, but there was a risk that copper prices would fall.
"In zinc and nickel we see prices rising, and more clearly in zinc," Outokumpu CEO Jyrki Juusela told a news conference, when asked about prospects for metals prices.
Outokumpu said the average zinc price in 1996 had been $0.46/lb, down from $0.47 in 1995. Nickel prices fell to $3.40/lb in 1996 from $3.73 in 1995. @

"(The price of) copper is (generally) forecast to rise during the next few years, but we think that there is a risk for a moderate fall in prices in coming years," Juusela said, adding the copper price was volatile and sensitive to changes in inventory levels.
The average 1996 copper price was $1.04/lb, down from $1.33 in 1995, Outokumpu said.
Earlier, Outokumpu said weaker metals prices caused its 1996 profit before extraordinary items and tax to fall to 229 million markka from 1.48 billion the previous year.
